# SB-1014 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Hazard description
------------------
Blasting operations adjacent to machining activities have produced airborne dust that migrates into the machining work envelope for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and surrounding fixtures. The airborne particulate is abrasive and can become embedded in chuck jaws and on tooling surfaces, increasing the risk of tool breakage, workpiece defects, and unexpected workholding failure during operation. Embedded abrasive particles in chuck jaw interfaces also raise the potential for concentricity loss and sudden loss of clamp force during a cycle. Inhalation exposure to fine particulates is an additional worker health hazard in shared work areas when local containment and extraction are not effective.

Background and rationale
------------------------
Recent inspections in line P1-L3 identified visible dust accumulation on the exterior of EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and on installed workholding. Root cause analysis linked the dust to adjacent blasting activities conducted without adequate containment or staged separation, allowing airborne solids to travel across the line. The presence of dust on mechanical interfaces degrades friction surfaces and can compromise fastener preload if particulates are lodged under head seating areas or between mating surfaces. The specified chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m; maintaining correct bolt preload is critical to clamp integrity. Contaminant ingress can cause bolt seating irregularities that reduce effective clamp preload even when torque is applied to specification, so controls focus on preventing ingress and documenting verification.

Affected equipment
------------------
- EQ-P1-L3-CN03 (Machining CNC turning center #3) and all workholding assemblies installed in its chuck jaws.  
- Tooling and fixtures stored or staged within the airflow path between blasting locations and line P1-L3 machining cells.  
- Adjacent process areas on line P1-L3 where dust migrates onto surfaces used for setup and inspection.

Required controls
-----------------
1. Containment and source control
   - All blasting operations feeding into areas that share air with line P1-L3 must use physical containment measures or sealed enclosures to prevent airborne particulate from reaching machining areas. Coordinate with blasting supervisors to confirm containment is in place before machining operations commence.
   - Use localized extraction at the blasting source to capture generated dust prior to migration.

2. Pre-operational inspection and cleaning
   - Before fitting workholding to EQ-P1-L3-CN03, visually inspect chuck jaw seats, jaw bolts, and mating surfaces for particulate and residue. Remove dry dust using brushes and low-pressure air blow-off directed away from personnel and electronics, followed by final wipe with lint-free cloths and approved cleaning agent per SOP-P1-L3-02.
   - Confirm that the seating surface for the jaw bolts is free of debris so that the specified chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is attainable and effective. When reassembling, apply the specified torque to the bolts and record completion.

3. Torque verification and documentation
   - Torque application to the specified clutch jaw bolt value must be performed using a calibrated torque tool. Record the application and sign the verification log. Calibration evidence should be available per maintenance records.
   - If bolt seating irregularity or dust contamination is discovered after torquing, disassemble, clean, re-seat, and re-torque to the specified value prior to release for operation.

4. Environmental controls in machining cells
   - Maintain local extraction and positive airflow patterns that reduce ingress of particulate into machining work envelopes. Monitor extraction performance and report deviations. Refer to SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-05 for air handling and housekeeping procedures related to P1-L3.

5. Work practices and training
   - Workers performing setup, maintenance, or blasting must be trained on the hazards of particulate migration and the procedures for containment, cleaning, and torque verification. Training completion shall be documented and available at the work area.
   - Avoid staging dirty fixtures or tooling near EQ-P1-L3-CN03. Segregate cleaned and ready-to-install workholding from items awaiting cleaning.

Examples and practical notes
----------------------------
- Example: A set of chuck jaws brought from an adjacent cell showed fine abrasive dust lodged under jaw bolt head seats. After initial torque application, radial runout increased. Disassembly, cleaning, and re-torqueing to the specified value restored clamp performance and concentricity. This illustrates the need to verify seating conditions, not only torque number application.
- Example: A temporary blast containment tarp with negative extraction was installed during a blasting campaign; subsequent checks on EQ-P1-L3-CN03 showed no new dust accumulation and routine torque checks confirmed stable jaw bolt preload.

Records to keep
---------------
- Pre-operational inspection checklist for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and related tooling, including a signed confirmation that chuck jaw bolt seating surfaces were cleaned.
- Torque verification log showing application of the specified chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m and the name of the person who applied and verified torque.
- Cleaning records and maintenance actions taken when contamination was found, including component inspection notes and reassembly verification.
- Training records for personnel involved in blasting, cleaning, and machining setup demonstrating completion of required instruction.
- Air extraction performance reports and any corrective actions initiated when extraction fell below acceptable performance, with references to SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-05.

References
----------
- SOP-P1-L3-02
- SOP-P1-L3-03
- SOP-P1-L3-05

Effective date
--------------
Effective upon issue; this bulletin is to be implemented immediately in line P1-L3 and incorporated into routine pre-operational checks for EQ-P1-L3-CN03.
